newsitem.title: LIBERIA: Peacekeepers in Liberia shut Sierra Leone frontier.
newsitem.headline: Peacekeepers in Liberia shut Sierra Leone frontier.

text.p: The ECOMOG African peacekeeping force in Liberia said on Monday its troops had sealed the land frontier with Sierra Leone and that naval units were patrolling coastal waters after the coup in Freetown.

The move coincided with growing confusion in Freetown after a coup by soldiers who battled Nigerian ECOMOG troops stationed in Sierra Leone. Freetown residents reported continuing resistance to the takeover and talk of a counter-coup.
Port officials and military sources in Monrovia said two naval boats left with hundreds of battle-ready ECOMOG troops on Sunday night, presumably heading for Sierra Leone.
Heavily armed Nigerian troops accompanied by tactical vehicles boarded the navy vessels, they said.

ECOMOG deputy force commander Brigadier-General Joe Kwateng told reporters in Monrovia that peacekeeping soldiers deployed in Liberia's western Grand Cape Mount county had been ordered to seal the Sierra Leone border.
"As part of the operation, soldiers of ECOMOG's navy battalion are continuing their patrol of international waters and have also stepped up border patrol," Kwateng said.
He declined to comment on the departure of boatloads of ECOMOG soldiers, but said: "The situation in Sierra Leone is an internal matter, but our men are there going about their assigned duties."

Hospital sources in Freetown said two Nigerian soldiers were among at least 18 people killed in Sunday's coup battles. ECOMOG's field commander General Victor Malu said in Lagos that his reports showed Nigerian troops had suffered no casualties.
ECOMOG sources said further reinforcements of peacekeepers were trucked to the Grand Cape Mount border region.

Reporters at the news conference saw more combat troops leaving in trucks. Military sources said they were heading for Bo Waterside, 90 miles (150 km) west of Monrovia or halfway to the Sierra Leone town of Kenema.

Lower rank soldiers seized power in Sierra Leone on Sunday, toppling elected President Ahmad Tejan Kabbah, who fled to neighbouring Guinea. Both Nigeria and Guinea have important contingents in the 10,000-strong ECOMOG force sent to Liberia in 1990 by the Economic Community of West African States.

ECOMOG has been policing Liberia since shortly after civil war erupted in December 1989 but Nigerian military ruler General Sani Abacha suggested last week that it should be transformed into a regional security force.
